title: FFT Applications Map
description: A two-by-three grid of six FFT application domains with icons; clicking a card reveals what the application does, which earlier chapter taught its underlying technique, and a capstone project idea in that domain.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Applications
Capstone Projects

educational.topic: Real-world FFT applications and the course techniques behind them
learningObjectives: Exemplify six domains where the FFT is central
Connect each domain to the chapter that taught its underlying technique
Identify a capstone project within a chosen domain
prerequisites: A working FFT on the target hardware

controls.label: Card
controls.purpose: Reveal description, chapter link and capstone idea

simulationModel.modelType: Static content map with click-to-reveal detail
assumptions: Each domain is attributed to the single chapter it leans on most, not to every chapter it touches
Capstone ideas are scoped to what a Pico 2 and the course's existing code can do
limitations: Six domains out of many; medical imaging, seismology and astronomy are not shown
One chapter link per domain, which understates how many techniques each really combines

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict the chapter link before revealing it, then convert a chosen domain into a testable capstone question
keyQuestions: Which chapter does each domain actually depend on?
Why is noise cancellation a phase problem rather than a magnitude problem?
commonMisconceptions: That these applications require techniques beyond the course
That noise cancellation is about amplitude matching
That radar is peak detection rather than correlation
assessmentOpportunities: Restate a capstone idea as a formal benchmark question
List what you would measure to know an implementation is correct rather than fast
